page: Microsoft Azure L8aos_v4 is a storage-optimized virtual machine powered by the AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance provides 8 virtual CPUs mapped across 4 dedicated physical cores with multithreading enabled at clock speeds reaching 3.7 GHz. The compute architecture includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache, backed by instruction set extensions including AVX-512, VNNI, and cryptographic accelerators like AES and SHA-NI.

Memory allocation stands at 64 GB, offering an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. The configuration features 5,760 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage, providing direct, high-capacity non-volatile storage without dedicated graphics accelerators. Benchmark results indicate strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng and Geekbench test suites, while overall multi-core and memory throughput metrics align with mid-range baselines. Although large uncached memory reads demonstrate lower bandwidth efficiency, small-block cached memory operations and text processing show elevated throughput.

The substantial NVMe solid-state capacity combined with balanced multi-threading delivers cost efficiency for I/O-intensive workloads, eliminating the need to attach secondary high-throughput volumes. Microsoft Azure L8aos_v4 is suited for transactional databases, distributed storage nodes, NoSQL databases like Redis or Cassandra, data warehousing caching layers, and search indexers requiring high local disk density alongside strong per-thread processing speeds.
description: Microsoft Azure L8aos_v4 is a storage-optimized virtual machine instance engineered for I/O-intensive workloads. It is driven by a 3.7 GHz AMD EPYC 9V74 processor offering 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores on an x86_64 architecture. The system provides 64 GB of system memory, yielding an 8 GB per vCPU ratio, paired with 5,760 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage. The configuration includes AVX-512 instruction support and omits dedicated GPUs. In benchmark evaluations, the L8aos_v4 demonstrates strong single-thread execution metrics in stress-ng and Geekbench tests, alongside standard multi-core processing throughput and solid small-block cache operations, despite lower bandwidth on large uncached memory reads. The inclusion of extensive high-speed NVMe storage provides solid resource density for database platforms, search index engines, distributed file systems, and heavy log aggregation tasks.
